newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ford to begin producing Ka cars in Brazil by Feb.
newsitem.headline: Ford to begin producing Ka cars in Brazil by Feb.

text.p: SAO PAULO, Dec 16 (reuter) - Ford Motor Co's Brazilian subsidiary will begin assembling its sub-compact Ka car at the company's Sao Bernardo do Campo plant by February, the firm's local chief said.
Ivan Fonseca e Silva, president of Ford Brasil, said the company plans to assemble 60,000 Ka cars a year in Brazil, the first sub-compact to be produced in the country.
"As of April, we will begin selling Ka cars in Brazil," Silva said, noting that small vehicles in Brazil account for 70 percent of total local car sales.

He did not say how much Ford planned to spend to produce the vehicle in Brazil, but added the investment would be small because the company would only have to convert its existing Fiesta asesembly line to produce the Ka.
The Ka is derived from the Fiesta, he said.
In the last two years, Ford has invested some $1.4 billion in Brazil out of a total $2.5 billion it plans to spend between 1995 and 2000.
The money was invested to modernize and restructure the Sao Bernardo plant and build a transmission and engine factory in Taubate, near Sao Paulo.
Ford, the fourth-largest car maker in Brazil with a market share of 10.4 percent, estimates annual car sales will grow to 180,000 units by 1998.
